stem: A 5-year-old girl is brought in because her teacher has noticed brief episodes of staring and ‘day-dreaming’ during class and choir practice. The episodes last a few seconds, the child immediately resumes activity afterward, and she has no post-ictal sleepiness, colour change, or developmental concerns. During the consultation, hyperventilation provokes a 5-second staring spell. You wish to confirm the diagnosis by EEG. What finding would you expect?

options.text: 3-4Hz spike and wave discharges during hyperventilation

explanation: This is typical childhood absence epilepsy. Absence seizures are classically provoked by hyperventilation and EEG shows generalized 3 Hz (often described as 3–4 Hz) spike-and-wave discharges.
rationale: The clinical vignette describes childhood absence epilepsy: brief staring spells, immediate recovery, normal development, and provocation by hyperventilation. The expected EEG finding is generalized 3–4 Hz spike-and-wave discharges.

optionExplanations.A: Seen in benign epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (rolandic epilepsy), not absence seizures.
optionExplanations.B: Associated with infantile spasms (West syndrome), which presents much earlier with developmental concerns.
optionExplanations.C: Typical of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, which causes multiple seizure types and developmental impairment.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: classic absence seizures show generalized 3–4 Hz spike-and-wave activity, often triggered by hyperventilation.

Instructions

Question 4 - 6 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 5-year old girl is brought in by her mother to see you because her teacher has been concerned that she has been having ‘day-dreams’ in choir practise and also during class. Her mother has also noted ‘day dreams’ which have been occurring mid-sentence associated with staring off in the distance. The ‘day dreams’ last a few seconds and then she is back to normal and continues on with her sentence. She doesn’t fall and doesn’t get sleepy after the events. She has no colour change. The girl is otherwise developmentally normal and got a good mid-year report from school. On examination her height and weight are on the 75

th

centile. She has a completely normal examination. You get the patient to blow up a balloon in your office and she has a staring spell that lasts 5seconds before she completely recovers.
